hints: Think about rate in terms of collision theory, particles need enough energy and the right orientation to react.
Notice that a lower $E_a$ means a bigger fraction of molecules already have enough energy, while higher temperature gives molecules more energy and more frequent collisions.
Check if more concentrated particles also collide more often, then see which combination includes all three true statements.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes reactions faster**

Rate increases when there are more frequent successful collisions. That means more collisions per second, or a greater proportion with energy $\ge E_a$.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{rate} \propto \text{frequency of successful collisions}$$

**Test statement 1: lower activation energy**

A lower $E_a$ lowers the energy barrier. So at the same temperature, many more molecules have energy greater than $E_a$. This is exactly what a catalyst does, so statement 1 is correct.

**Test statement 2: higher temperature**

Increasing temperature makes particles move faster, so collisions are more frequent. More importantly, a much larger proportion of molecules have energy $\ge E_a$. So statement 2 is correct.

**Test statement 3: higher concentration**

More reactant particles in the same volume means they are closer together. Collision frequency increases, so more successful collisions per second occur. So statement 3 is correct.

Conclusion: 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct, because all three statements are true. Lower $E_a$, higher temperature and higher concentration all increase the frequency of successful collisions and therefore increase rate.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination includes only 1 and 2. It wrongly leaves out statement 3, but increasing concentration definitely increases collision frequency and rate.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination includes only 2 and 3. It wrongly leaves out statement 1, but a lower activation energy increases the proportion of successful collisions and is a key way to speed up a reaction.
options.D: Incorrect. This includes only statement 1. It misses that temperature and concentration are also standard ways to increase rate through more energetic and more frequent collisions.
